title: Reduce tail latency via cooperative windowing and proactive KV warmup
creator: Ava Chen
description: Triage summary: production traces show recurrent tail spikes (p99) in short-chat workloads caused by rare long-running scheduling windows and cold KV cache reads during bursty ingress. This ticket implements two coordinated refactors: (1) a cooperative windowing model for the continuous batcher that fragments oversized windows into cooperative micro-windows to avoid monopolizing the reactor thread, and (2) a proactive KV warmup adapter that observes recent sequence prefixes and issues low-priority prefetches to the KV backend before commit. The aim is to reduce p99 tail latency and variance without impacting throughput or increasing memory pressure significantly.
acceptance_criteria:
- p99 generation latency for short-chat synthetic workload reduced by >=35% in staging versus current baseline (baseline p99 420ms -> target <=273ms).
- KV cold-read rate (misses leading to >5ms backend read) reduced by >=50% on same workload.
- No regression (>3%) in aggregate token/sec throughput during 30m soak test.
- Canary rollout shows no increase in error rate or OOM events.
- New metrics and tags added: batch_window_fragments, kv_prefetch_hit, kv_warmup_backpressure.
- Code covered by unit tests + integration stress harness + documented design doc link.
technical_notes:
Design highlights: implement a cooperative-window scheduler that tracks per-worker budget (ms) and yields at micro-window boundaries. Micro-windows are sized by observed token distribution heuristics (adaptive using EWMA). The scheduler will prefer breaking windows at prefix-safe boundaries (complete request boundaries or token-affine cutpoints) to preserve KV prefix locality.

KV warmup adapter: lightweight predictor watches recent request prefixes and maintains an LRU of hot prefix candidates. Prefetches are scheduled on a low-priority I/O lane with rate limits and backpressure tied to KV queue length to avoid overload. Prefetches carry a TTL and are eligible for soft eviction under memory pressure.

Dependency upgrades: bump liburing to 2.2 for async poll improvements (reduces syscall latency), upgrade jemalloc to 5.3 for fragmentations observed in long-running runners. Validate ABI compatibility in the perf job.

Telemetry: add timers for micro-window durations, a histogram for prefetch latency, and a KV warmup hit-rate gauge. All metrics carry the route/model tag to help per-model analysis.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature branch + unit tests. 2) Perf benchmarking in CI harness (compare baseline). 3) Merge behind feature-flag 'coop_window_kv_warmup'. 4) Deploy to staging and run 4-hour soak with synthetic short-chat and long-chat mixed workload. 5) Canary to 5% on non-critical region for 6 hours, monitor p50/p95/p99 and OOMs. 6) Ramp to 25% for 24 hours, then 100% if stable.

Rollback: feature flag off; if rollback fails, revert merge and re-deploy previous runtime artifact.
metrics: Key dashboards: runtime/latency (p50/p95/p99), kv/warmup/hit_rate, batcher/window_fragment_count, host/mem/used, host/threads_blocked. Alert thresholds: p99 up 20% -> page oncall; kv_warmup_backpressure > 0.7 for 5m -> investigate.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: aggressive prefetching could increase backend load and mask real cache behavior. Mitigation: start with conservative prefetch budget, tie to KV queue depth, add kill-switch in adapter.

Risk: window fragmentation could increase context-switch overhead. Mitigation: micro-window sizing uses EWMA with floor to avoid pathological tiny windows; measure CPU delta in perf job.

Risk: dependency upgrade exposes subtle allocator behavior in long-lived processes. Mitigation: shadow run with jemalloc profiling for 24h before canary.
